findings.summary: Round 1 LOW: the --owner-authorization-ref argparse help text still named only evidence-errata and owner-reassignment while the enforced gate correctly admitted supersede. Corrected in the one-hunk follow-up commit; round 2 verified the delta is exactly that help string and re-ran the 201-test suite OK.

The '-supersede-' branch-name gate is substring-based, the identical pre-existing idiom used by pause/resume/close/transfer/authorize; every substantive gate (delta, states, receipt, checkpoint, owner ref) still binds.

A non-canonical-case id in superseded_by is verified closed via the casefolded claim lookup, consistent with how all claims are keyed; it cannot satisfy the replacement requirement on its own because PACKAGE_RE refuses it at claim level. No gate bypass.
A non-list superseded_by iterates per-character in the intent gate and produces noisy per-character refusals - fail-closed, not exploitable.

Residual assumption, not a defect: the receipt-absence gate reads origin/main's current tip and relies on the standing invariants that governed merges always leave receipts, control transitions change only claim paths, and direct pushes to main are blocked by Azure policy. A compound upstream governance breach deleting a receipt from main is outside this package's threat model.
